q: In which year was Queen Elizabeth II crowned at Westminster Abbey?
fact: She became queen in February 1952, but the coronation took place on 2 June 1953. Many British families bought their first TV set to watch it.

q: Which 1957 treaty created the European Economic Community?
fact: It was signed in March 1957 by six countries: Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and West Germany.

q: In which year was the armistice that stopped the Korean War signed?
fact: The armistice was signed on 27 July 1953. No peace treaty followed, so the two Koreas are technically still at war.

q: Which two climbers made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest in 1953?
fact: They reached the summit on 29 May 1953. Mallory and Irvine vanished near the top in 1924, and nobody knows whether they made it.

q: What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957?
fact: The Soviet Union launched it on 4 October 1957. It was about the size of a beach ball and sent out radio beeps that anyone could pick up.

q: 'The Day the Music Died' in February 1959 was a plane crash that killed Ritchie Valens, The Big Bopper and which star?
fact: The crash happened in Iowa on 3 February 1959. Don McLean's 1971 song 'American Pie' gave the day its name.

q: Which 1959 epic starring Charlton Heston won 11 Academy Awards?
fact: Its 11 Oscars were a record that stood alone until Titanic matched it in 1998.

q: Audrey Hepburn won an Oscar for playing a runaway princess in which 1953 film?
fact: It was her first leading role in a Hollywood film, and it won her the Academy Award for Best Actress.

q: Which young Hollywood star died in a car crash in 1955, aged 24, before two of his three starring films were released?
fact: Rebel Without a Cause came out a month after his death and Giant the year after. Both of his Oscar nominations came after he died.

q: Which film star married Prince Rainier III in 1956 and became Princess of Monaco?
fact: She married Prince Rainier in April 1956 and gave up acting at the age of 26.

q: Which song gave Elvis Presley his first US number one hit, in 1956?
fact: It was his first single for RCA Records and made him a national star in the spring of 1956.

q: Which TV comedy starring Lucille Ball was America's top-rated show for much of the 1950s?
fact: It was the top-rated show in America in four of its six seasons, and it helped make filming sitcoms with three cameras in front of a live audience the norm.

q: Which country won the 1958 FIFA World Cup, with a 17-year-old Pelé scoring in the final?
fact: The tournament was held in Sweden. Brazil beat the hosts 5-2 in the final, and Pelé scored twice.

q: Which Norwegian city hosted the 1952 Winter Olympics?
fact: Norway topped the medal table, and speed skater Hjalmar 'Hjallis' Andersen won three gold medals.

q: Who became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes, in 1954?
fact: He ran 3:59.4 in Oxford on 6 May 1954. His record lasted only 46 days before John Landy beat it.

q: Which toy, created by Ruth Handler and named after her daughter, made its debut at the New York Toy Fair in 1959?
fact: Barbie was named after Handler's daughter Barbara. Ken, launched in 1961, was named after her son.

q: In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick described the structure of what?
fact: Their double helix model was published in April 1953. It built on X-ray images made by Rosalind Franklin.

q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
fact: Construction began overnight on 13 August 1961. The wall stood for 28 years.

q: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
fact: For 13 days in October 1962, the USA and the Soviet Union came closer to nuclear war than at any other time.

q: Martin Luther King Jr. gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963 in front of which memorial?
fact: He spoke on 28 August 1963 to about 250,000 people at the March on Washington.

q: Norway's oil age began in 1969 with the discovery of which North Sea field?
fact: Phillips Petroleum found Ekofisk just before Christmas 1969, and production started in 1971.

q: Who became the first human in space, in April 1961?
fact: On 12 April 1961 he orbited the Earth once in Vostok 1. The flight lasted 108 minutes.

q: What was the name of the Apollo 11 lunar module that landed on the Moon in 1969?
fact: 'The Eagle has landed,' Armstrong radioed on 20 July 1969. Columbia was the command module that stayed in orbit with Michael Collins.

q: The world's first human heart transplant was carried out in 1967 in which country?
fact: Christiaan Barnard performed it in Cape Town on 3 December 1967. The patient, Louis Washkansky, lived for 18 days.

q: On which TV show did the Beatles make their famous US debut in February 1964?
fact: Around 73 million Americans watched on 9 February 1964.

q: Which music festival took place on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York, in August 1969?
fact: Around 400,000 people came to Max Yasgur's farm. Jimi Hendrix closed the festival on the Monday morning.

q: Which artist first showed his 32 paintings of Campbell's Soup cans in 1962?
fact: There was one canvas for each of the 32 soup flavours Campbell's sold at the time. They were first shown in Los Angeles.

q: Which was the first James Bond film, released in 1962?
fact: Sean Connery played 007, and Ursula Andress walking out of the sea became one of cinema's most famous scenes.

q: Which 1965 musical starring Julie Andrews is set in Salzburg, Austria?
fact: It won Best Picture and passed Gone with the Wind to become the highest-grossing film of its time.

q: Who famously sang 'Happy Birthday, Mr. President' to John F. Kennedy in 1962?
fact: She sang at Madison Square Garden in May 1962, less than three months before she died.

q: Which 1960s model, born Lesley Hornby in London, was named 'The Face of 1966'?
fact: She was only 16 when her photos launched her career.

q: In 1964, which 22-year-old beat Sonny Liston for the world heavyweight title and soon took the name Muhammad Ali?
fact: Liston did not come out for the seventh round, and the new champion shouted 'I am the greatest!'

q: Which country won the 1966 FIFA World Cup on home soil?
fact: England beat West Germany 4-2 after extra time at Wembley, and Geoff Hurst scored a hat-trick.

q: In October 1969, the first message was sent over ARPANET, the forerunner of the internet. What did it say?
fact: The team at UCLA tried to type 'LOGIN', but the system crashed after two letters.

q: The lava lamp was invented in 1963 in which country?
fact: A British accountant, Edward Craven Walker, launched it as the Astro Lamp.

q: Which US president resigned in 1974 because of the Watergate scandal?
fact: He resigned in August 1974 and is still the only US president to have done so. Gerald Ford took over.

q: In which year did Saigon fall, ending the Vietnam War?
fact: North Vietnamese tanks entered Saigon on 30 April 1975. US combat troops had already left in 1973.

q: Who became the United Kingdom's first female prime minister in 1979?
fact: She won the election in May 1979 and stayed in office for eleven and a half years.

q: The world's first 'test-tube baby', Louise Brown, was born in 1978 in which country?
fact: She was born in Oldham, England, on 25 July 1978. Robert Edwards later won the Nobel Prize for developing IVF.

q: Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Ronald Wayne and who else?
fact: Their first product, the Apple I, was built by hand and sold for $666.66.

q: Which supersonic airliner began carrying passengers in 1976?
fact: British Airways and Air France started Concorde flights on 21 January 1976. It could fly from London to New York in about three and a half hours.

q: Which Swedish group won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo'?
fact: The contest was held in Brighton, England. ABBA went on to become one of the best-selling acts in pop history.

q: Which Queen song from 1975 runs almost six minutes and has no repeating chorus?
fact: The record label thought it was too long for radio. It topped the UK chart for nine weeks anyway.

q: The first Star Wars film (1977) was later given which subtitle?
fact: It opened in May 1977 simply as 'Star Wars'. 'Episode IV – A New Hope' was added for the 1981 re-release.

q: Which 1975 Steven Spielberg film is often called the first summer blockbuster?
a: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
fact: The mechanical shark kept breaking down, so Spielberg showed it far less than planned, which made the film scarier.

q: Which actor played Vito Corleone in The Godfather (1972)?
fact: Brando won Best Actor but refused the Oscar in protest at how Hollywood portrayed Native Americans.

q: Which actor danced his way to fame as Tony Manero in 'Saturday Night Fever' (1977)?
fact: The film's Bee Gees soundtrack became one of the best-selling albums of all time.

q: Which reggae legend released the album 'Exodus' in 1977?
fact: In 1999, Time magazine named Exodus the best album of the 20th century.

q: At the 1976 Montreal Olympics, which 14-year-old gymnast scored the first perfect 10?
fact: The scoreboard could not show 10.00, so it displayed 1.00.

q: The 1974 'Rumble in the Jungle' boxing match took place in which country?
fact: Muhammad Ali beat George Foreman in Kinshasa with his 'rope-a-dope' tactic. Zaire is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

q: Which Swedish tennis star won five Wimbledon titles in a row, from 1976 to 1980?
fact: His winning run ended in the 1981 final, when John McEnroe beat him.

q: Which Norwegian runner won the New York City Marathon nine times, starting in 1978?
fact: She won her first New York marathon in 1978 in a world-record time.

q: Which puzzle, invented by a Hungarian professor in 1974, became a worldwide craze?
fact: Ernő Rubik built it as a teaching tool. It reportedly took him about a month to solve it himself.

q: Which company launched the Walkman portable cassette player in 1979?
fact: The first Walkman, the TPS-L2, went on sale in Japan in July 1979.

q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
fact: The border opened on the night of 9 November 1989, after an East German spokesman mistakenly said the new travel rules applied immediately.

q: Which Soviet leader introduced the policies of glasnost and perestroika in the 1980s?
fact: Glasnost means openness and perestroika means restructuring. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1990.

q: In which year did Gro Harlem Brundtland become Norway's first female prime minister?
fact: Her first term lasted eight months. She returned as prime minister in 1986 and again in 1990.

q: The 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster happened in which then-Soviet republic?
fact: Reactor 4 exploded on 26 April 1986. Sweden's Forsmark nuclear plant raised the first alarm in the West after detecting radiation.

q: In which year did the Space Shuttle Challenger break apart shortly after launch?
fact: It broke apart 73 seconds after launch on 28 January 1986. The teacher Christa McAuliffe was among the seven crew.

q: The 1985 Live Aid concerts took place in London and which US city?
fact: Phil Collins played at both concerts on 13 July 1985, flying across the Atlantic on Concorde in between.

q: Which Norwegian band topped the US charts in 1985 with 'Take On Me'?
fact: The pencil-sketch music video helped the song reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in October 1985.

q: Which album, released in 1982, is widely cited as the best-selling album of all time?
fact: Michael Jackson's album is estimated to have sold around 70 million copies.

q: Which Norwegian duo gave Norway its first Eurovision win, in 1985, with 'La det swinge'?
fact: Hanne Krogh and Elisabeth Andreassen won in Gothenburg. Seven years earlier, Norway had famously scored zero points.

q: Which 1982 Steven Spielberg film features an alien who wants to 'phone home'?
a: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
fact: E.T. overtook Star Wars to become the highest-grossing film of its time.

q: In 'Back to the Future' (1985), what speed must the DeLorean reach to travel through time?
fact: The time machine also needs 1.21 gigawatts of electricity, supplied first by plutonium and later by a bolt of lightning.

q: In which 1984 film does Arnold Schwarzenegger first say 'I'll be back'?
fact: James Cameron made the film on a budget of about 6.4 million dollars.

q: Where did Lady Diana Spencer marry Prince Charles in 1981?
fact: Around 750 million people around the world watched the wedding on 29 July 1981.

q: Which pop star released the album 'Like a Virgin' in 1984?
fact: She performed the title song at the first MTV Video Music Awards in 1984, wearing a wedding dress on top of a giant cake.

q: Who scored the 'Hand of God' goal against England at the 1986 World Cup?
fact: Four minutes later he scored the 'Goal of the Century' after dribbling past five England players. Argentina went on to win the tournament.

q: In the 1980 'Miracle on Ice', the US ice hockey team beat which country at the Lake Placid Olympics?
fact: The team of American college players won 4-3, then beat Finland to take the gold.

q: Apple launched the Macintosh in 1984 with a famous Super Bowl ad inspired by which novel?
fact: The ad was directed by Ridley Scott and was shown nationally only once, during the Super Bowl in January 1984.

q: Which arcade game from 1980 was originally called 'Puck-Man' in Japan?
fact: The name was changed for the US market, partly because vandals could easily change the P to another letter.

q: Which falling-blocks game did Alexey Pajitnov create in Moscow in 1984?
fact: He made it on a Soviet Elektronika 60 computer. It became a worldwide hit on the Nintendo Game Boy in 1989.

q: In which year was Nelson Mandela released from prison?
fact: He walked free on 11 February 1990 after 27 years in prison, and became South Africa's president in 1994.

q: In which year did the Soviet Union officially dissolve?
fact: Gorbachev resigned on 25 December 1991, and the Soviet flag over the Kremlin was lowered that evening.

q: In which year did the United Kingdom hand Hong Kong back to China?
fact: The handover took place at midnight on 30 June 1997. Portugal handed Macau back to China in 1999.

q: In 1994, Norway held a referendum on joining the European Union. What was the result?
fact: It was the second time Norwegians said no. A 1972 referendum had also rejected membership.

q: In which year did the Channel Tunnel between England and France open?
fact: It opened on 6 May 1994. The tunnel is about 50 km long, and nearly 38 km of it runs under the sea.

q: What was the name of the sheep that became the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, in 1996?
fact: She was born in Scotland in July 1996 and named after the singer Dolly Parton.

q: Which company did Larry Page and Sergey Brin found in 1998?
fact: The search engine was first called BackRub. The name Google comes from 'googol', the number 1 followed by 100 zeros.

q: Which British girl group had a worldwide hit with 'Wannabe' in 1996?
fact: Wannabe reached number one in more than 30 countries.

q: What was the name of the coffee shop in the TV series 'Friends'?
fact: Friends ran for ten seasons, from 1994 to 2004.

q: Which book was first published in the UK in June 1997?
a: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
fact: The first print run was only 500 hardback copies. Several publishers had turned the book down before Bloomsbury said yes.

q: Which 1997 film won 11 Oscars and became the first film to earn over one billion dollars worldwide?
fact: Its budget of around 200 million dollars was also a record at the time.

q: Which 1994 film features the line 'Life was like a box of chocolates'?
fact: Forrest Gump won six Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Actor for Tom Hanks.

q: What is the name of the island in 'Jurassic Park' (1993)?
fact: It is a fictional island off Costa Rica. Isla Sorna, the 'Site B' island, appears in the sequels.

q: In which city did Diana, Princess of Wales, die after a car crash in 1997?
fact: The crash happened in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel on 31 August 1997. Her funeral was one of the most-watched TV broadcasts ever.

q: Which singer launched her career with '...Baby One More Time' in 1998?
fact: She was 16 when the song was released in October 1998.

q: Which Norwegian town hosted the 1994 Winter Olympics?
fact: Norway won 26 medals on home snow, more than any other country.

q: With which team did Michael Jordan win six NBA championships in the 1990s?
fact: He won two 'three-peats' with Chicago: 1991-93 and 1996-98.

q: Which country won the 1998 FIFA World Cup on home soil?
fact: France beat Brazil 3-0 in the final at the Stade de France, with two headers from Zinedine Zidane.

q: Which golfer won the 1997 Masters by a record 12 strokes, aged just 21?
fact: He became the youngest Masters champion, and his winning margin is still a Masters record.

q: On 1 January 2002, how many EU member states swapped their old currencies for euro notes and coins?
fact: Greece joined the eurozone in 2001, just in time to be one of the twelve. Sweden and Denmark kept their own currencies.

q: Barack Obama was elected in 2008 as which number US president?
fact: He took office in January 2009 as the first African American president.

q: In the EU's biggest-ever enlargement, in 2004, how many countries joined at once?
fact: Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and the three Baltic states were among the countries that joined on 1 May 2004.

q: Which social network did Mark Zuckerberg launch from his Harvard dorm room in 2004?
fact: It launched in February 2004 as TheFacebook and was open only to Harvard students at first.

q: In which year did Apple introduce the first iPhone?
fact: Steve Jobs presented it in January 2007 as 'an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator'.

q: In which year was Wikipedia launched?
fact: It went online on 15 January 2001, a date now celebrated as Wikipedia Day.

q: YouTube's first video, 'Me at the zoo' (2005), was filmed at which zoo?
fact: Co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded the 19-second clip on 23 April 2005. He is standing in front of the elephants.

q: In 2006, astronomers reclassified which planet as a 'dwarf planet'?
fact: The International Astronomical Union made the decision in August 2006, leaving the solar system with eight planets.

q: Which singer released the album 'Back to Black' in 2006?
fact: She won five Grammy Awards in a single night in February 2008.

q: Which British TV talent show from 2001 was remade as 'American Idol' in 2002?
fact: Norway got its own Idol in 2003. The winner, Kurt Nilsen, went on to win World Idol.

q: Which Norwegian violinist and singer won Eurovision 2009 with 'Fairytale'?
fact: 'Fairytale' scored 387 points in Moscow, a record at the time.

q: Which actor played Captain Jack Sparrow in 'Pirates of the Caribbean' (2003)?
fact: Depp has said he based the character partly on Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards.

q: Which film won all 11 Oscars it was nominated for, at the 2004 Academy Awards?
a: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
fact: It matched the record of 11 Oscars held by Ben-Hur and Titanic, and was the first fantasy film to win Best Picture.

q: Which actor played the Joker in 'The Dark Knight' (2008) and won an Oscar after his death?
fact: Ledger died in January 2008, before the film opened. He won Best Supporting Actor the following year.

q: Which 2001 film about a green ogre won the first-ever Oscar for Best Animated Feature?
fact: The award was handed out for the first time in 2002, and Shrek beat Monsters, Inc. to win it.

q: In which city did Usain Bolt set the 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, in 2009?
fact: His 9.58 took more than a tenth of a second off his own record of 9.69 from the Beijing Olympics.

q: Which swimmer won a record eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
fact: He beat Mark Spitz's record of seven golds at one Games, set in Munich in 1972.

q: Which Norwegian biathlete won all four men's biathlon events at the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympics?
fact: He ended his career with 13 Olympic medals, 8 of them gold.
